findings.message: The shared api-check adapter's HTTP handler only serves add and greet. The R2 and R4 api checks therefore prove only the task assertions plus a generic HTTP 200 response, not divide or clamp over HTTP. This is a limit of the shared adapter and the acceptance tests were not weakened. Reproduce by reading examples/api-check.mjs lines 59-65.
clamp does not validate min <= max or NaN inputs, and add does not validate types. This is outside R1-R4 text and acceptance assertions.

The R1/R2 and R3/R4 backlog executions use two different attempt_ids (c6861861... and 9a1f3c52...), consistent with an interruption and resume. Whether the SDK runtime records for both attempts were imported is for the parent's final verify to confirm. The Read-only tools gave no way to correlate them.
Runtime drain, burst finish, state end and the final Opus audit are later steps. This review does not cover them.
